headline: Discussed park panhandling signs, a grant transfer to Bristol Health, and an October 24, 2026 drug take-back day; approved May minutes.
summary: Members reported 14 overdose deaths from January 1, 2026 to date and discussed the grant transfer to Bristol Health. They also discussed park issues, a brochure, and upcoming drug take-back and empty chair events. The group approved the May 11, 2026 minutes.
decisions: Approved the May 11, 2026 minutes; motion carried, all in favor.

plain_text:
Mayor’s Opioid Task Force Meeting 
September 21, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. 
City Hall | 111 N Main Street | Bristol, CT 06010 
Rm 310 
MINUTES (DRAFT UNTIL APPROVED) 
 
In Attendance: 
Ellen Zoppo-Sassu Mayor 
Steven Seymour City Council District 3 
Teran Chapis Mayor’s Aide 
Lucas Amoroso-Whittles The Bristol Edition 
Jade Bray Bristol Hospital Behavioral Health Services 
Jessica Mastropiero Bristol Burlington Health District (zoom) 
Phyllis Delmastro (Zoom) 
Lt. Eric Hanson Bristol Police 
Officer Monica Finkle Bristol PD Community Resource Officer 
Stephen Bynum Bristol Youth & Community Services 
Sandy Kamens  
Christy Knowles   
Donna Friday  
Maria Theam Recording Secretary 
 
1. Call to Order and Member Introduction: 
The meeting was called to order at 5:02 p.m. followed by Introductions. 
2. Approval of May 11, 2026 Minutes: 
    Motion to Approve Minutes – by Steven Seymour 
    2nd Motion – Lt. Eric Hansen 
    All in favor – I – Motion Carries – Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu 
3. Update Items 
a. Bristol Police Wellness Officers: 
Officer Finkle discussed the Police Department’s efforts to offer treatment resources to 
individuals they encounter and suggested that the Police Department participate in future 
Warming Center meetings to help ensure coordination among the involved agencies. 
It was reported that Brian’s Angels will be closing its current location at the end of the month 
because its lease was not renewed. The individuals previously served at that location have been 
dispersed to other agencies throughout the City, and Brian’s Angels has not yet secured a new 
location.
Discussion followed regarding ongoing issues within City parks. Federal Hill is currently under 
control; however, Brackett Park continues to present concerns. The Mayor discussed signage 
intended to discourage panhandling and encourage individuals to donate through appropriate 
organizations rather than directly to panhandlers. The signs have been remade and will be 
reinstalled in various plazas throughout the City. 
Lt. Hanson reported that the Police Department has increased enforcement efforts in response to 
these concerns. 
b. B.E.S.T: Stephen Bynum reported that they will be participating in the Mum Festival this 
weekend. He also noted that an employee recently resigned and they are currently working to 
address the vacancy. 
Mr. Bynum stated that the current grant ends on September 29 and that they are not eligible to 
reapply. Discussion followed regarding the Youth Coalition and Adult Coalition, including 
where those initiatives may fit moving forward and whether they could be incorporated into the 
Opioid Task Force. It was noted that funding remains available through the opioid settlement 
funds. 
c. Mayor’s Update: Discussion was held regarding the Task Force’s past efforts and initiatives 
aimed at reducing the stigma associated with substance use. 
4. New Business: Jessica Mastropietro reported that there have been 14 overdose deaths from 
January 1, 2026 to date, compared with 35 deaths in the past. She also discussed the transfer of 
the grant to Bristol Health and plans to contract with EMS to provide recovery coaches who will 
respond to active overdose incidents. She stated that more concrete information regarding the 
program is expected to be available within the next month. 
5. Old business: 
 a. reprinting of brochure – The Mayor reviewed the proposed brochure that will be left 
by the Police Department following calls involving an overdose. Discussion was held regarding 
the availability of testing strips. Jessica Mastropietro reported that hundreds of testing strips are 
currently available through the Department of Public Health (DPH) and that there is no need to 
purchase additional strips at this time. Should the current supply be depleted, opioid settlement 
funds could potentially be used to purchase additional strips. 
The Mayor continued reviewing the proposed brochure and stated that it will be distributed to 
Task Force participants for review. Suggested additions included the tips line, information 
regarding Live LOUD, and an interactive resource map. 
6. Announcements: Lt. Hanson reported that Drug Take Back Day and Vape Take Back Day 
will be held on October 24, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., rain or shine. Both events will 
take place on the same day, with efforts also being coordinated with the schools. ReWorld will 
handle the recycling of collected vaping devices. It was also reported that the vape detection 
alarms in the schools are now operational. A permanent drug take-back container is available in 
the Police Department lobby.
It was noted that the Zoning Commission will meet tonight at 6:00 p.m. to review, discuss, and 
consider adoption of a moratorium concerning the establishment or expansion of vape shops in 
the City. 
Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu discussed the 10th Annual Nationwide Empty Chair Campaign, which 
will take place from September 25 through October 2 in the green area between the Police 
Department and the Post Office. Community members may display a chair in memory of a loved 
one lost to an overdose. 
7. Adjournment:  
 Motion to Adjourn at 5:53pm – Steven Seymour 
 2nd Motion – Lt. Eric Hansen 
All in favor – I – Motion Carries – Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu 
 
        Respectfully Submitted, 
         
Maria Theam   
Recording Secretary
